item.title: To the editor: Labor perception, population are related
item.description: Gov. Mike Dewine has disputed a recent study predicting a decline in Ohio’s population in the next couple decades. Toledo Mayor Kapszukiewicz has chimed in that such a decline could be attributed to the Republican domination of state politics.

item.title: Editorial: GOP poll revealing
item.description: Republican politicians are overwhelmingly hostile to solar energy following the lead of Donald Trump, but Republican voters overwhelmingly support solar energy when the technology is an all-American product, according to the pollster used by Trump’s presidential campaigns.

item.title: Toe the line: How dancing can lead to a healthier lifestyle
item.description: When Marilyn Campbell discovered line dancing, it reverberated with her like a tuning fork.

item.title: Seeing red: U.S. measles elimination status at risk as contagious virus continues to spread
item.description: The United States’ measles eradication status may be dropped this year as the country has been pounded by a resurgence of the highly contagious virus since January of 2025.

item.title: Paul R. Hollenbeck, 1946-2026: Toledo architect left mark on cityscape
item.description: Paul R. Hollenbeck, a noted Toledo architect, died Jan. 29 in Chicago. He was 79.

item.title: Shribman: Black Americans were fighting 2 wars
item.description: His grandparents and mother were born in Selma, Ala., the site of the violence of the 1965 civil rights march that led to the Voting Rights Act. He grew up in Columbus where within 30 yards of his house six Black active-duty soldiers went off to Vietnam, including one of his childhood heroes — a young man who one day quietly slipped off to war. item.title: Walton: For The Blade building, it’s end of an era
item.description: The presses have been silent for many years, their rumble a distant but wonderful memory. The beautiful noise, the busy clatter of hundreds of people assembling what some of us affectionately called the “Daily Miracle,” has gone away. Soon, all that will be left of the grand old building at the corner of Superior and Orange streets in downtown Toledo will be the emptied out shell of a place that has lived beyond its time.

item.title: Editorial: Wishing for doom?
item.description: Observing Black History Month to honor the contributions and stories of African-Americans in the United States is an appropriate exercise by the Lucas County Commissioners. Running the Pan-African flag up the flagpole outside Government Center — not so much, especially given the remark made by one participant.

item.title: Harden scores 23 in Cavaliers debut, Mitchell leads with 35 in 132-126 win over Kings
item.description: SACRAMENTO, Calif. — James Harden scored 23 points in his Cavaliers debut and Donovan Mitchell had 35 to lead Cleveland to a 132-126 victory over Sacramento on Saturday night, sending the Kings to their 12th straight loss.
